sourceFramework: Scripture, the supplied Martyrs’ Mirror, and the supplied Anabaptist Church History exhibit; source-specific disagreements are recorded without replacing that faith-history framework.
photoPublicationPolicy: Research provenance only. These photographs and painting reproductions are not public-site illustrations or build assets.
method: Visual inspection of all eight overview panels and six branch photographs, with actual-pixel crops for caption text; mapping to curated records, source accounts, and new narrative records.

scope.overviewCaptions: Every lettered caption and the unlettered dated statistics block is inventoried.
scope.branchLabels: All prominent named branch lines and named leader lines are inventoried.
scope.chartMicroannotations: Additional small central annotations are inventoried separately with legibility flags; unreadable text is never supplied from inference.
scope.yellowBorders: Explicit surrounding-context disposition, not an exhaustive transcription of secular/church-history microtext.

overviewPanels.caption: A
overviewPanels.title: Jesus Christ
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: The resurrected Jesus is presented as Lord and Savior, and the beginning and end of the cyclorama.
overviewPanels.notes: The overview gives a faith claim and date, not a cited Scripture passage.

overviewPanels.caption: B
overviewPanels.title: Calvary – Empty Tomb
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Crucifixion/three crosses of Good Friday and the empty tomb of Easter.

overviewPanels.caption: C
overviewPanels.title: Apostle Peter
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Peter holds the keys and cross; after Pentecost he preached and baptized 3,000 new believers.
overviewPanels.notes: Acts-related subject; Acts 2 is not explicitly printed in this caption. Do not treat the lifespan as an independently established historical date.

overviewPanels.caption: D
overviewPanels.title: Constantine
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Emperor uses the cross, protects Christian worship through the Edict of Milan (313), and establishes Constantinople as the eastern capital.
overviewPanels.notes: Political ruler/church-state context, not an Anabaptist faith branch.
overviewPanels.scope_note: Retained in the source inventory as surrounding church/world context. A stand-alone biography or general-history narrative is outside this Anabaptist/Radical Reformation site’s present scope.

overviewPanels.caption: E
overviewPanels.title: State Church
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Gradual alignment of church and state; adoption and enforcement of sacraments.
overviewPanels.scope_note: Retained in the source inventory as surrounding church/world context. A stand-alone biography or general-history narrative is outside this Anabaptist/Radical Reformation site’s present scope.

overviewPanels.caption: F
overviewPanels.title: Churches / Monasteries Formed
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Monastic prayer and service; monastery complexes, church structures and cathedrals.
overviewPanels.notes: General institutional church history, not a named Anabaptist predecessor community.
overviewPanels.scope_note: Retained in the source inventory as surrounding church/world context. A stand-alone biography or general-history narrative is outside this Anabaptist/Radical Reformation site’s present scope.

overviewPanels.caption: G
overviewPanels.title: St. Patrick
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Conversion of the Irish to Christianity in the fifth century.
overviewPanels.notes: Keep displayed 430–461 as the panel date; the caption does not say whether it is a lifespan or ministry range.
overviewPanels.scope_note: Retained in the source inventory as surrounding church/world context. A stand-alone biography or general-history narrative is outside this Anabaptist/Radical Reformation site’s present scope.

overviewPanels.caption: H
overviewPanels.title: St. Boniface
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: England-born missionary to Germanic tribes; patron saint of Germany.
overviewPanels.scope_note: Retained in the source inventory as surrounding church/world context. A stand-alone biography or general-history narrative is outside this Anabaptist/Radical Reformation site’s present scope.

overviewPanels.caption: I
overviewPanels.title: Peter Waldo
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Vernacular New Testament translation, poverty/almsgiving and public preaching; excommunication and caption-reported burning of 80 Waldensians in Strasbourg (1212); refuge in Alps.
overviewPanels.notes: Relevant pre-Reformation dissent/reform context. Photo alone does not establish a continuous institutional genealogy to sixteenth-century Anabaptists.

overviewPanels.caption: J
overviewPanels.title: The Crusades
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: First Crusade (1095), capture of Jerusalem (1099), Children’s Crusade (1212), seven crusades and increased papal power as described by panel.
overviewPanels.notes: Religious/political/military context, not a nonresistant Anabaptist branch.
overviewPanels.scope_note: Retained in the source inventory as surrounding church/world context. A stand-alone biography or general-history narrative is outside this Anabaptist/Radical Reformation site’s present scope.

overviewPanels.caption: K
overviewPanels.title: John Wyclif
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: English Bible from Vulgate (1382), vernacular preaching and church/clergy reform; followers called Lollards; declared heretic in 1415 and body/books ordered burned.
overviewPanels.notes: Preserve source spelling Wyclif; possible canonical normalization requires a separate authority.

overviewPanels.caption: L
overviewPanels.title: John Hus
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Czech-language preaching, ethical/clergy reforms, influence of Wyclif; summoned to council at Konstanz (1414), imprisoned, tried and burned; followers later formed Moravian Church per panel.
overviewPanels.notes: Caption’s Czechoslovakia is an outdated geography label. Do not silently treat it as a current place name, or conflate Moravian Church with Hutterites in Moravia.

overviewPanels.caption: M
overviewPanels.title: Printing Press Invented
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Movable type; Gutenberg Bible (1455); production of books, manuscripts, tracts and indulgences.
overviewPanels.notes: Technology/source-dissemination context. The body’s 1455 is outside the overview header 0–1436 AD; printed dates need external corroboration before authoritative use.
overviewPanels.scope_note: Retained in the source inventory as surrounding church/world context. A stand-alone biography or general-history narrative is outside this Anabaptist/Radical Reformation site’s present scope.

overviewPanels.caption: A
overviewPanels.title: Johann Tetzel
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Indulgence preaching/promoting leads to Luther’s response in the narrative.
overviewPanels.scope_note: Retained in the source inventory as surrounding church/world context. A stand-alone biography or general-history narrative is outside this Anabaptist/Radical Reformation site’s present scope.

overviewPanels.caption: B
overviewPanels.title: Ulrich Zwingli
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Ordination (1506), Zurich pastorate (1519); Swiss-German preaching from Matthew, Acts and Epistles; reforms to mass/communion (1525); death in war of Kappel (1531).
overviewPanels.notes: Magisterial reformer/formation context. Body directly names Acts; he must not be labeled an Anabaptist.
overviewPanels.scope_note: Retained in the source inventory as surrounding church/world context. A stand-alone biography or general-history narrative is outside this Anabaptist/Radical Reformation site’s present scope.

overviewPanels.caption: C
overviewPanels.title: Martin Luther
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: 95 Theses (1517), challenge to papal authority, Bible as source of revealed knowledge and salvation as free grace through Jesus Christ.
overviewPanels.notes: Reformation context; not a Radical Reformation or Anabaptist branch.
overviewPanels.scope_note: Retained in the source inventory as surrounding church/world context. A stand-alone biography or general-history narrative is outside this Anabaptist/Radical Reformation site’s present scope.

overviewPanels.caption: D
overviewPanels.title: Bible Study in Zurich
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Lay Bible study groups are described as the start of the Swiss Brethren in 1522.

overviewPanels.caption: E
overviewPanels.title: Young Radicals
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Grebel and Manz invited to translate original Latin, Greek and Hebrew texts; former parish priest Blaurock later joined.
overviewPanels.notes: No independent year printed in this caption; do not invent a date.

overviewPanels.caption: F
overviewPanels.title: Menno Simons
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Menno consecrated as a Catholic priest in 1524.
overviewPanels.notes: Direct biography background of a later Anabaptist leader; at the event shown he is still a Catholic priest.

overviewPanels.caption: G
overviewPanels.title: Swiss Brethren
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Disagreement over reform and infant baptism; public debate and council order to baptize children or leave Zurich; meeting in mother of Manz’s home; Blaurock asks for baptism on confession of faith and then baptizes others.
overviewPanels.notes: The mother is unnamed. Photo calls this the first recorded Anabaptist adult baptism; no individual baptizer of Blaurock is named in the caption.

overviewPanels.caption: H
overviewPanels.title: Bolt Eberli
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Arrest after preaching at St. Gall; death by fire; described as first Anabaptist martyr of the Swiss Brethren.
overviewPanels.notes: Exact spelling is Bolt Eberli on this overview. Do not silently substitute another known name or date.

overviewPanels.caption: I
overviewPanels.title: Death of Leaders
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Grebel dies in exile of plague (1526); Manz and Blaurock imprisoned; Blaurock flogged/banished; Manz sentenced to drowning in Limmat (January 5, 1527).

overviewPanels.caption: J
overviewPanels.title: Blaurock Martyred
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Blaurock continues preaching/baptizing; captured and burned with fellow believer Hans Langegger at Klausen.

overviewPanels.caption: K
overviewPanels.title: Brotherly Union of Schleitheim
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Secret gathering; Brotherly Union statement; Sattler leads discussion and drafts what becomes the Schleitheim Confession of Faith.

overviewPanels.caption: A
overviewPanels.title: Michael Sattler
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Arrest/imprisonment after Schleitheim; civil and religious disobedience charges; torture and burning (May 21 as printed); wife drowned eight days later.
overviewPanels.notes: Wife is unnamed. Preserve printed day as source evidence rather than silently correcting; authoritative public history requires corroboration. Place appears as Rottenberg on panel.

overviewPanels.caption: B
overviewPanels.title: Anabaptists in Nikolsburg
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Refuge under Lords of Lichtenstein; perhaps 12,000 Anabaptists; war-tax and violence debates; Hut’s nonviolence versus Hubmaier’s acceptance of sword for political rulers; divisions lead to Stäbler eviction.
overviewPanels.notes: Political protectors and war against Turks are context inside a direct branch-development entry. Preserve distinction between the two Anabaptist positions.

overviewPanels.caption: C
overviewPanels.title: Balthasar Hubmaier
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Arrest after departing Nikolsburg, interrogation/torture, charges of heresy and treason, burning in Vienna.

overviewPanels.caption: D
overviewPanels.title: Hans Hut
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Evangelist, repeated arrest/trial in autumn 1527, death in cell fire before formal sentence; corpse sentenced and burned following day.

overviewPanels.caption: E
overviewPanels.title: Melchior Hoffman
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Furrier and early Luther supporter; conversion in Strasbourg; movement spread to northwest Germany/Netherlands; followers called Melchiorites; arrest in Strasbourg (1533), expectation of Christ’s return, death in prison.
overviewPanels.notes: Hoffman is the overview spelling; do not conflate Melchiorites with all Anabaptists.

overviewPanels.caption: F
overviewPanels.title: Stäbler Shared Goods
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: After eviction, group assembles at Bogenitz and shares possessions on a cloak; common property becomes a Hutterite tenet.

overviewPanels.caption: G
overviewPanels.title: Ausbund
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Hymn core written in prison (1535–1540); earliest imprint 1564; grows to 140 hymns, unnotated and orally transmitted; continued Amish use as reported by panel.
overviewPanels.notes: 1564 lies outside this overview’s 1527–1536 header. “Oldest continuously used hymnal” is a source claim requiring independent verification if used publicly.

overviewPanels.caption: H
overviewPanels.title: Hutterites in Moravia
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Establishment in Moravia (1529), Hutter’s leadership (1533), relocation planning and settlement of differences at Auspitz; bruderhof colonies; adoption of Hutter’s name; return to Tyrol under threat, arrest/torture, burning (February 25, 1536 as printed).
overviewPanels.notes: Place of execution is not separately named beyond the Tyrol narrative. Exact day is transcription, not independent verification.

overviewPanels.caption: I
overviewPanels.title: Sicke Freerks Snijder Execution
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Snijder baptized on confession of faith and executed for re-baptism; Menno studies Scripture and becomes convinced of believers’ baptism.

overviewPanels.caption: J
overviewPanels.title: Anabaptists in Münster
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Millennial expectation, Münster as New Jerusalem, armed movement, siege by bishop, city’s fall in July 1535 as printed, massacre/executions and bodies in iron cages.
overviewPanels.notes: In scope as a divergent violent/apocalyptic episode that shaped subsequent Anabaptist history; do not present it as equivalent to the nonresistant Swiss/Mennonite/Hutterite lineages. Date and evaluative wording are panel claims.

overviewPanels.caption: K
overviewPanels.title: Menno Simons Ordained
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: After Münster, Menno studies Scripture on baptism, Lord’s Supper and worship; public commitment (January 30, 1536), leaves priesthood and works underground; delegation asks him to become elder/bishop and he accepts.
overviewPanels.notes: Heading says ordained 1536; body dates public commitment specifically, then describes acceptance of leadership without a separate ordination date. Do not merge these into a more precise unsupported date.

overviewPanels.caption: A
overviewPanels.title: Anabaptist Leadership
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Regional leadership: Marpeck in south Germany/France; Philips in Prussia; Menno in Netherlands/north Germany.

overviewPanels.caption: B
overviewPanels.title: Hutterites Banished
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Imperial edict expels Hutterites from communal homes; winter refuge in forests and caves.
overviewPanels.notes: Ferdinand is the political actor in a direct persecution/migration story, not a faith exemplar or branch.

overviewPanels.caption: C
overviewPanels.title: Departures
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Philips withdraws (1540), weary of Münsterite fanaticism; former German priest Pastor ordained elder (1542) and banned from Anabaptists (1547) over views of Christ.
overviewPanels.notes: “Heretical” is the panel’s evaluative characterization; if reused, attribute rather than making an unqualified doctrinal judgment.

overviewPanels.caption: D
overviewPanels.title: Hutterite Golden Age
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Communal flourishing, schools/early childhood education, pottery/agriculture; about 100 bruderhof farm colonies and 20,000–30,000 members as reported; sympathetic Maximilian II and leadership of Walpot.
overviewPanels.notes: Internal chronology conflict: heading 1555–1560 precedes body’s reign 1564–1576 and leadership 1565–1578. Do not silently harmonize. Population and colony counts are panel estimates.

overviewPanels.caption: E
overviewPanels.title: Aid to Calvinists and Menno’s House
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Mennonite aid to ice-bound refugee ship at Wismar (1553–54); Menno and family sheltered on estate near Oldesloe; illness/death and garden burial (January 31, 1561); linden tree and printing house traditionally associated with him.
overviewPanels.notes: Photo explicitly hedges the tree as “supposedly” planted by Menno and house as “believed” place of printing; preserve that uncertainty.

overviewPanels.caption: F
overviewPanels.title: Leenaert Bouwens
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Ordained elder by Menno at Emden (1551), preaching/baptism travel; records 10,252 baptisms from 1551–1582; many congregations originate from work.
overviewPanels.notes: 10,252 is exactly the panel number, not an independently checked count.

overviewPanels.caption: G
overviewPanels.title: Hans Haslibacher
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Imprisonment, exile and property confiscation; return/arrest/torture; vision of beheading and three signs; Ausbund poem; last Anabaptist martyr executed in Canton Bern as described.
overviewPanels.notes: Vision and “last execution” are claims in the caption; distinguish tradition from verified event chronology.

overviewPanels.caption: H
overviewPanels.title: Hutterite Chronicles
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Braitmichel starts official chronicle in 1560; accounts through 1542; his death (1573); continuation by Hauptrecht Zapft through 1665; supplement by Waldner (1749–1824) covers 1665–1755.
overviewPanels.notes: Book title appears “Geshicts-Buch” on the overview; this orthography and the proper names should be independently corroborated before canonical normalization. Dates extend well beyond panel header.

overviewPanels.caption: I
overviewPanels.title: Plunder of Hutterites
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Turkish wars beginning 1605 bring killing/captivity; Thirty Years War and disease devastate region; Peace of Westphalia (1648).
overviewPanels.notes: Keep direct effects on Hutterites in scope; the general war/political history is surrounding context, not another Anabaptist branch.

overviewPanels.caption: J
overviewPanels.title: Icy Rescue by Dirk Willems
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Prison escape over ice; returns to rescue pursuing guard; re-arrest and secure bell-tower imprisonment; burned on May 16, 1569.
overviewPanels.notes: Guard is unnamed. Rescue/martyrdom is directly relevant to nonresistance and the Martyrs Mirror framework; overview itself does not cite a book page.

overviewPanels.caption: K
overviewPanels.title: Smyth & Robinson
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Smyth/Robinson congregations leave England for Amsterdam (1607–08); Smyth followers join Mennonite congregation; Robinson to Leiden (1609); Helwys returns England (1612), leading toward General Baptists.
overviewPanels.notes: In scope as a named cross-branch connection. Do not flatten General Baptists or Puritans into Mennonite branches or assert a direct lineage beyond the described connection.

overviewPanels.caption: L
overviewPanels.title: Dordrecht Confession
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Peace Convention adopts 18-statement “A Declaration of the Chief Articles of Our General Christian Faith”; 51 Flemish/Frisian preachers sign (1632); Alsace adoption (1660), later Palatinate adoption, Pennsylvania adoption (1725); continued Amish/some conservative Mennonite recognition.
overviewPanels.notes: Caption L continues at the top of the fourth text column above M; a single-column extraction would miss adoption dates and branches.

overviewPanels.caption: M
overviewPanels.title: Martyrs Mirror
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Compiled by Mennonite elder van Braght (1660) to recover foreparents’ faith; 1685 second edition includes 104 Luyken etchings; Dutch original, German publication at Ephrata (1749), English edition at Lampeter Square (1837).
overviewPanels.notes: Explicit historical source/framework anchor. Research photos and pictured murals/etchings are not authorized public illustration assets. This is a source-history summary, not independent verification of every edition detail.

overviewPanels.caption: N
overviewPanels.title: Hutterite Ordnung
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Ehrenpreis becomes vigorous leader after community disruption; elected bishop (1639); writes community-life regulations and restores internal discipline (1651).
overviewPanels.notes: Lifespan is abbreviated “1589–62” exactly as printed; avoid silently replacing the ambiguous abbreviation in transcription.

overviewPanels.caption: O
overviewPanels.title: Banishment
overviewPanels.visible_content_summary: Anabaptist Commission (1659), arrest/forced-conversion-or-departure policy with 14-day deadline; about 700 men, women and children banished from Bern to Palatinate (1671).
overviewPanels.notes: Caption reports capital punishment had ceased; this is persecution/migration history, not a generic secular milestone.
